proofs.proof_tex:
Let a certificate be returned, and first work in the normalized parameterization.  By \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), every \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) has the unique normalized representative \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\in\mathcal I_H\), and
\[
 O_H^N(\eta)=O_H(\theta),\qquad
 T_{a,H}^N(\eta)=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{1}
\]
Every transition used to obtain the certificate is admitted only after the exact local obligations in \(\textnormal{def:sa-csid-machine}\) have succeeded.  We record why these obligations are sufficient.  At a selector transition, the stored zero--one multiplexer equation makes replacement by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\), followed by substitution of \(x_s\) in the children, an equality of the two context-kernel polynomials modulo the inherited gate and coordinate-copy constraints.  This rewrite creates no divisor.  At a fixing transition the successor is \(K'_{s,D}=K_{s,D}/m_{s,W}\), and the verified identity is
\[
 m_{s,W}K'_{s,D}=K_{s,D}.
\tag{2}
\]
At a sum or district transition, the corresponding expanded identity is likewise verified after multiplication by all reduced denominators.  The positivity ledger makes every such multiplication reversible on the registered branch domain.  Induction over the finite returned transition log therefore shows that its final labelled circuits represent the same observation--target relation as the initial normalized circuits on that domain.  This uses only the exact polynomial identities required by the four transition definitions; it does not infer an identity from graphical eligibility alone.

Consider a formula certificate.  Write the accepted residual candidate as \(F_H=P/D\), where \(D\) is the product of its sign-normalized reduced denominators.  Reduction to zero modulo the current finite constraint list \(\mathcal J=(J_1,\ldots,J_M)\) means that the verifier has polynomial multipliers \(h_1,\ldots,h_M\) for which the formal identity
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=\sum_{j=1}^M h_jJ_j
\tag{3}
\]
holds componentwise.  For \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\in\mathcal I_H\), every inherited constraint \(J_j(\eta)\) is zero by the construction of the current constraint list from \(\mathcal I_H\).  Thus the right side of (3) vanishes at \(\eta\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\), every selector normalizer, fixing margin, and admitted elimination denominator is strictly positive at \(O_H^N(\eta)=O_H(\theta)\).  Consequently
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H,
\qquad
 D\{O_H^N(\eta)\}>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Division of (3) by the positive value in (4), followed by (1), gives
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}
 =F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}
 =T_{a,H}^N(\eta)
 =T_{a,H}(\theta)
\quad(\theta\in\Theta_H).
\tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(F_H\) has domain \(\mathfrak D_H\), so (5) makes no assertion at an ambient table outside that domain.

Now consider a negative certificate and fix \(b\in\mathcal B_H\).  Let \(\eta_b^+\) and \(\eta_b^-\) denote the two normalized primitive records to which the residual transition applies \(\rho_H\).  This application is well typed only on \(\mathcal I_H\), because \(\rho_H:\mathcal I_H\to\Theta_H\); hence an admitted and returned residual transition has
\[
 \eta_b^+,\eta_b^-\in\mathcal I_H,
 \qquad
 \theta_b^\pm:=\rho_H(\eta_b^\pm)\in\Theta_H.
\tag{6}
\]
Concretely, the verifier establishes (6) by its primitive-simplex signs, the equalities in the retained constraint list, the selector-mass signs
\[
 s_H^N(\eta_b^\pm)(s)>0\iff s\in H,
\tag{7}
\]
and strict positivity of every admissible observation polynomial.  Thus neither support nor root-factorization membership is inferred merely from observed-law equality.

The two remaining accepted residual obligations are polynomial equality of all supported observed coordinates and a target-difference polynomial of certified nonzero constant sign on the open rational box.  Therefore
\[
 O_H^N(\eta_b^+)=O_H^N(\eta_b^-),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^-).
\tag{8}
\]
Applying the two inverse identities from \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) to (6)--(8) yields
\[
 O_H(\theta_b^+)=O_H(\theta_b^-),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}(\theta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^-).
\tag{9}
\]
Finally, membership in \(\Theta_H\) in (6), together with \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\) and \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\), says that both models have selector support exactly \(H\) and every structurally admissible supported cell is strictly positive.  Equations (4)--(5) and (6)--(9) prove the two asserted soundness alternatives.

Fix a positive certificate and \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), put \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\), and suppose that \(\mathbf p_H\) lies in the differentiable interior of the branch domain \(\mathfrak D_H\).  Let \(C=\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\).  The finite-alphabet assumption makes \(m_H=|C|<\infty\), and for \(X_i=(V_i,S_i)\),
\[
 \widehat{\mathbf p}_H=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n e_{X_i}^C,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{p_H}(e_{X_i}^C)=\mathbf p_H.
\tag{1}
\]
The domain is described by finitely many strict inequalities in coordinates and registered polynomials, all continuous.  Interiority therefore supplies a relative neighborhood \(N\) of \(\mathbf p_H\) in the simplex and \(\delta>0\) such that the relative \(\ell_\infty\)-ball of radius \(\delta\) lies in \(N\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\).  Since
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H(c)\}
 =\frac{p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}}{n},
\]
coordinatewise Chebyshev inequalities and a finite union bound give
\[
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\notin N\}
 \le
 \frac1{n\delta^2}\sum_{c\in C}p_H(c)\{1-p_H(c)\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(\Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\notin\mathfrak D_H\}\to0\).

All registered denominators are positive on a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(\mathbf p_H\).  The finite rational circuit \(F_H\) consequently has a continuously differentiable ambient-coordinate extension there.  Differentiability, (1), and the bound
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_H}\left\|\sqrt n
 (\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)\right\|_2^2
 =\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)
 -\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}<\infty
\]
give, on the event in (2),
\[
 F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)
 =J_H(\mathbf p_H)(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H-\mathbf p_H)
 +o_p(n^{-1/2})
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{IF}_H(X_i)+o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{3}
\]
The influence function has mean zero by (1), and it has finite variance because \(C\) is finite.  The same differentiability expansion along every interior multinomial submodel proves regularity of this local smooth plug-in.  Therefore \(\textnormal{lem:asymptotic-linear-normality}\), applied after premultiplication by a fixed \(c\in\mathbb R^{k_Y}\), yields
\[
 \sqrt n\,c^{\mathsf T}
 \{F_H(\widehat p_H)-F_H(p_H)\}
 \rightsquigarrow
 N\bigl(0,c^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Hc\bigr).
\tag{4}
\]

On the reporting event, direct expansion of the defined empirical influence functions gives
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H
 =J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)
 -\widehat{\mathbf p}_H\widehat{\mathbf p}_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\widehat{\mathbf p}_H)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{5}
\]
The empirical table converges in probability to \(\mathbf p_H\) by (2), and the Jacobian of a rational circuit is continuous where its registered denominators are nonzero.  Hence
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_H\longrightarrow
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)
 \{\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf p_H)-\mathbf p_H\mathbf p_H^{\mathsf T}\}
 J_H(\mathbf p_H)^{\mathsf T}
 =\Sigma_H
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{6}
\]
The last equality follows by taking the variance of the influence function in (3).

Certificate soundness gives \(F_H(p_H)=Q_{a,H}\).  Fix \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\) and take \(c=e_y^Y\) in (4).  If
\[
 v_{H,y}:=(e_y^Y)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H e_y^Y>0,
\]
then (6) implies \(\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}\to1\) in probability and \(\Pr(\widehat v_{H,y}>0)\to1\).  Thus
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat Q_{a,H}(y)-Q_{a,H}(y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat v_{H,y}}}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1).
\tag{7}
\]
For clarity, the studentization in (7) follows directly from (4) and (6): on \(\{|\widehat v_{H,y}/v_{H,y}-1|\le\varepsilon\}\), compare the statistic with the two fixed rescalings by \((1\pm\varepsilon)^{-1/2}\), use continuity of the normal distribution function, and then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).  The quantile definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\), (2), and (7) now imply
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 Q_{a,H}(y)\in CI_y\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]

For a fixed nonzero \(\lambda\) with \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_H\lambda>0\), take \(c=\lambda\) in (4) and premultiply (6) by \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\lambda\).  The identical comparison argument gives
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_{p_H}\{\widehat p_H\in\mathfrak D_H,
 \lambda^{\mathsf T}Q_{a,H}\in CI_\lambda\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (8)--(9) concern respectively one fixed outcome component and one fixed scalar contrast.  Off \(\mathfrak D_H\), the procedure returns \(\bot_H\) and reports no interval.  Since the neighborhood in (2) depends on the fixed interior law, the proof makes no claim of uniform coverage as a cell probability or registered denominator approaches zero.

Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_H\) and set \(p_H=O_H(\theta)\).  We induct over the finite canonical order in which denominators are admitted to the branch ledger.

For a context \(s\in H\), the initialization denominator is
\[
 p_H(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}p_H(v,s).
\tag{1}
\]
Exact support, \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), makes the left side positive.  Equivalently, the sum is nonempty and each of its structurally admissible summands is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\).  Selector rewriting itself introduces no further division by \(\textnormal{def:selector-transition}\).

Suppose all entries earlier than an admitted fixing margin are positive.  Its eligibility certificate, required by \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\), writes it as
\[
 m_{s,W}(p_H)
 =\frac{\sum_{c\in B}p_H(c)}
 {\prod_{j\in J}d_{H,j}(p_H)},
\tag{2}
\]
where \(B\subseteq\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\) is nonempty and every \(j\in J\) precedes this margin.  The numerator of (2) is strictly positive by admissible-cell interior positivity, and the denominator is strictly positive by the induction hypothesis; the empty-product case equals one.  Hence \(m_{s,W}(p_H)>0\).

After cancellation and sign normalization, an admitted rational-elimination denominator has, by \(\textnormal{def:elimination-transition}\), an exact ledger factorization
\[
 d(p_H)=r
 \prod_{j\in J_0}d_{H,j}(p_H)
 \prod_{k\in J_1}
 \left\{\sum_{c\in B_k}K_k(p_H,c)\right\},
 \qquad r\in\mathbb Q_{>0},
\tag{3}
\]
where the entries indexed by \(J_0\) are earlier selector or fixing denominators, every \(B_k\) is nonempty, and the ledger certifies each displayed kernel cell as branch-reachable and positive.  Every factor in (3) is therefore positive: this follows from the induction hypothesis for the first product and from the certified positivity and nonemptiness for each sum in the second product.  Thus \(d(p_H)>0\).

Finite induction proves that every member of \(\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}}\) is positive at \(p_H\), while (1) and admissible-cell interior positivity establish all branch-required cell inequalities.  The definition of \(\mathfrak D_H\) now gives \(O_H(\theta)\in\mathfrak D_H\).  Since \(\theta\) was arbitrary,
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\]
Every step is pointwise at the chosen \(\theta\); no common positive lower bound was introduced.

Define
\[
 \mathcal R_H=
 \left\{\theta\in\Theta(G^+):
 \operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\quad
 p_\theta(c)>0\ \text{for every }c\in
 \mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
All probabilities in (1) are well defined because \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\) gives finite alphabets and the recursive SCM definition supplies \(p_\theta\).  By the definition of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\), its members satisfy the common recursive order, declared independent-root factorization, known selector multiplexers, and full canonical response-table parameterization, before either restriction in (1) is imposed.  By \(\textnormal{def:model-class}\), \(\Theta_H\) imposes precisely this common syntax together with the two restrictions in (1).  Hence
\[
 \Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap\mathcal R_H
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\tag{2}
\]
If the published class contains a parameter violating either restriction in (1), that parameter belongs to the right side of (2) but not the left side, proving strictness under the stated premise.

By the definition of the support-exact global twin relation,
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 =\{(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\Theta_H^2:
 O_H(\theta^+)=O_H(\theta^-),\ 
 T_{a,H}(\theta^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta^-)\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking Cartesian squares in (2) and using (3) gives
\[
 \mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}
 \subseteq\Theta_H^2
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(w=(\theta^+,\theta^-)\in\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\).  If either coordinate \(\theta^\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}\), assigns positive selector mass to some \(s_0\notin H\), then \(\theta^\varepsilon\notin\Theta_H\) by \(\textnormal{ass:exact-selector-support}\), so (3) implies \(w\notin\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  If instead some \(c_0\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\) has \(p_{\theta^\varepsilon}(c_0)=0\), then \(\theta^\varepsilon\notin\Theta_H\) by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\), and the same conclusion follows.  Finally, if equality fails on a coordinate of \(O_H\), then \(O_H(\theta^+)\ne O_H(\theta^-)\), which directly violates (3).  Thus each of the three displayed defects excludes the pair from the fixed-support global twin relation.

The definition of \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) does not add exact support \(H\), positivity on every cell in \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\), or equality of the complete map \(O_H\).  Membership in that relation alone therefore does not imply membership in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  If it contains a pair with any one of the three defects, that pair belongs to
\[
 \mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}
 \setminus\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}},
\]
which proves \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\not\subseteq\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove that the fixed machine, from its input alone, schedules a simulation of every successful support-licensed Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser derivation and therefore actually returns the translated formula.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen initial state does not define a worklist of recursive tasks or an input-determined compiler that creates and regenerates the selector, ancestor-restriction, district-splitting, and prescribed-fixing agenda. The existing token transition rules verify a supplied token but do not prove that the token required by the published recursion is present. Consequently the step-by-step algebraic translation proves existence of a valid trace, not return by the deterministic machine.
open_obligations.attempted: Translated context initialization, gate substitution, fixing quotients, marginalization, and district factorization and proved equality of all translated kernels. This closes algebraic preservation and denominator positivity, but the earlier trace-installation route was rejected because it would make the successful published derivation part of the machine input.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any fixed successful support-licensed published derivation, gate substitution, reachable fixing, marginalization, and district factorization can be translated step by step into equal normalized rational kernels.  Every translated divisor is positive by \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\), and gate reinsertion plus \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\) transports the terminal formula to \(T_{a,H}\).  What is not yet proved is that the frozen input-determined machine necessarily schedules this translated derivation.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove nonresidual progress and termination of the intended recursive task computation, including district splitting into multiple child tasks, from one compiler determined solely by the normalized input.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen state \(\zeta\) has one global random mask and token lists but no unfinished tasks of the required form, while the frozen measure \(\mu_H\) does not order a worklist or the multiple child tasks created by a recursive district split. The machine also does not construct the initial or successor agenda. Thus the definitions prove that every admitted move decreases, but do not exclude a nonresidual state with no supplied eligible token.
open_obligations.attempted: Checked each of the four local cross-multiplied identities and the displayed lexicographic decrease. A well-foundedness proof rules out an infinite admitted sequence. It cannot establish the stronger no-stuck conclusion because preloading a desired trace, choosing an arbitrary fixable vertex, or treating absence of a token as residual-ready would violate the fixed input-determined compiler directive.
open_obligations.partial_result: Every admitted transition satisfies its local relation-preservation identity on the registered positive domain, and every admitted transition strictly decreases the displayed \(\mu_H\); hence an admitted transition sequence is finite.  This does not establish nonresidual progress from the frozen initial state because no recursive unfinished-task compiler or regenerated agenda is defined.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derive the claimed four-transition execution from the machine's canonically compiled initial and regenerated agendas.
open_obligations.obstruction: The numerical twin and every named local eligibility check can be verified, but \(\textnormal{def:worked-execution}\) does not specify the fields of the initial state \(\zeta_0\), and \(\textnormal{def:sa-csid-machine}\) has no input-determined token compiler. A construction sentence saying that the encoded trace occurs cannot itself prove that the schedule produces the required tokens in that order.
open_obligations.attempted: Verified the response-simplex inequalities, exact observed-cell cancellation, exact selector support, strict positivity, target contrast, and individual selector, fixing, elimination, and residual eligibility. The remaining trace claim was not inferred from the hand-built token list.
open_obligations.partial_result: The response perturbation \(d=(-4,-1,0,3)\) on \(0<b<1/32\) stays inside the binary response simplex, preserves all six \((S,A,Y)\) cells, leaves selector support \(H=\{0,1\}\), and changes the target by \(-b/2\).  At \(b=1/64\), the common cell vector is \((13,11,13,11,24,24)/96\) and the targets are \(1/2\) and \(63/128\).  The four named local transitions are individually eligible for the displayed hand-built trace, but the frozen machine does not define an initial or regenerated agenda from which that trace follows.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove both nonresidual progress and that every irreducible normalized residual has either a verifier-encoded rational identifying circuit or a verifier-encoded support-exact global-twin box.
open_obligations.obstruction: The first gap is the missing recursive task compiler identified for \(\textnormal{thm:transition-soundness-termination}\). Independently, \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\) remains unresolved: finiteness of the projection and contrast lists does not imply that one candidate passes, and the frozen core supplies no theorem excluding an identified observation-fiber functional that is algebraic but nonrational.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved that a returned formula implies fiber constancy and that a returned twin implies nonidentification, as well as uniqueness of an accepted scheduled successor and finiteness of any admitted execution. Did not replace the required dichotomy by a formula/twin/stuck trichotomy or install an oracle trace.
open_obligations.partial_result: Soundness gives the two one-way implications: a returned formula is constant on every \(O_H\)-fiber, while a returned global-twin box proves failure of identification.  The fixed priority makes any accepted successor unique, and the decreasing measure makes every admitted execution finite.  The missing steps are nonresidual progress and the all-residual rational-formula-or-common-contrast theorem posed by \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Compile every ordinary recursive ID success into the frozen projection library and every ordinary hedge failure into the frozen rational-affine categorical global-twin library, with verifier certificates.
open_obligations.obstruction: The laid-back normalized graph and the nonresidual transition algebra do reduce to the ordinary semi-Markovian setting, but no frozen definition or established lemma proves that the residual lists contain all ordinary ID formulas and hedge witnesses. The needed hedge construction must handle arbitrary finite alphabets, independent-root factorization, equality through all observed descendants, a common positive rational interior mixture, persistent target contrast, and exact encoding in the verifier's candidate format.
open_obligations.attempted: Established almost-sure constancy of the selector, equality of the ordinary and normalized observed--target relations, and reduction of the fixing and elimination primitives. A generic appeal to classical formula-or-hedge completeness was not used because it would not prove candidate-list inclusion or the required rational support-preserving compiler.
open_obligations.partial_result: When \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), exact support makes \(S=s_{\emptyset}\) almost surely; laid-back gate normalization gives the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\), and \(\Phi_H\) becomes its ordinary observational--interventional relation.  The frozen selector, fixing, and elimination primitives reduce algebraically to their ordinary counterparts.  The remaining formula-or-hedge claim requires a proof that every ordinary ID terminal formula and every categorical hedge twin is present in, and accepted from, the frozen residual candidate lists.
